title: Secrets: HashiCorp Vault, Sealed Secrets and SOPS

videos.script: Everything in the cluster comes from Git. A token cannot, not as it is, because everybody who reads the repository would read the token. {{problem}} This lesson tries three ways out. Sealed Secrets encrypts a secret so that only your cluster can open it. {{sealed}} SOPS encrypts the values and leaves the keys readable, so a review still shows what changed. Flux decrypts it on the way in. {{sops}} Then Vault, which keeps the secret out of Git altogether. You run the real server, not the dev one, and watch it come back sealed after a restart. {{vault}} Last, Vault learns to trust the cluster. A pod proves who it is with the token Kubernetes already gave it, and gets one path it may read. Nothing else. {{identity}}
